title: Helical Domain-Wall-Ring Networks Reshape Superconducting Correlations
abstract: Extended domain-wall networks emerging in moiré materials provide a distinct platform for quasi-one-dimensional electronic states. However, the interaction-driven orders in confined networks remain largely unexplored. Here, we discuss superconducting (SC) correlations in interacting helical domain-wall-ring networks that emerge in the closed topological domains formed within the moiré patterns of an underlying twisted bilayer honeycomb lattice. We first analyze the system within the framework of an infinite-size theory and show that inter-ring SC-pair tunneling is renormalization-group relevant and thus enhances SC correlations through inter-ring phase locking. To address finite-size effects resulting from the ring-network geometry, we present a self-consistent variational approach. Our analysis shows that even in the regime where the infinite-size theory predicts strongly-coupled pair tunneling, the induced phase-locking scale remains strongly suppressed. In contrast, the SC scaling dimension continues to decrease with decreasing twist angle and remains insensitive to the pair-tunneling strength, revealing a qualitative mismatch from the infinite-size expectation. This discrepancy demonstrates that ring networks do not simply approach their infinite-size counterparts but can exhibit qualitatively distinct collective behavior. Our study highlights how the interplay of confinement effects and ring-network geometry can reshape SC correlations.
summary: The paper theoretically analyzes superconducting correlations in helical domain-wall-ring networks found in moiré materials. It contrasts predictions from idealized infinite systems with results obtained using a self-consistent variational method for finite rings. The key finding is that the ring geometry leads to qualitatively different collective behavior, suggesting confinement effects are crucial and cannot be ignored.
main_problem: The study investigates how superconducting (SC) correlations are reshaped by confinement effects within helical domain-wall-ring networks compared to predictions from infinite-size models.
main_result: Finite-size ring networks exhibit qualitatively distinct collective behavior, as the SC scaling dimension evolution does not simply follow the strong-coupling predictions derived for infinite systems.
method: The analysis combines Renormalization Group (RG) theory for initial insights with a self-consistent variational approach to handle finite-size effects in the bosonic field description of the system.
model_or_system: The physical platform is superconducting correlations within helical domain-wall-ring networks arising from moiré patterns in twisted bilayer honeycomb lattices. The model uses Luttinger Liquid theory for intra-ring physics and includes inter-ring tunneling terms.

paper_structure: The paper progresses through establishing bosonic field representations, deriving effective low-energy actions via perturbation theory (second order in tunneling), applying a variational minimization procedure to find self-consistent parameters ($m_J$), and finally calculating the SC correlation function ($\eta_{	ext{SC}}$).
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed theoretical framework for understanding how geometric confinement fundamentally alters many-body quantum phenomena, which is crucial knowledge when designing artificial superconducting circuits or moiré heterostructures.
